summary: Original site of a c.1936 Forestry Commission Aermotor tower near Eastover, Richland County; sold and moved in 1995; sources disagree on where it stands now.

facts.design: 120-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with 7 by 7 foot steel cab
facts.status_note: Sold and moved from this site in 1995; sources disagree on where the tower stands now

access.note: Private property; the register lists Ray Littlejohn as owner and describes no public access

events.note: Built around 1936 as a 120-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower, named Eastover Tower by the SC Forestry Commission
SC Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993 (system-wide)
Sold and moved to private property; the register says Dr. Ken Huggins bought it and moved it to family property
Sold by Dr. Ken Huggins to Ray Littlejohn; the register says it had yet to be moved after the sale

corrections.why: Both sources say the tower was sold and moved away from the original Eastover site to private property

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower moved to family property in 1995, yet also says it had yet to be moved after the 2007 sale; a magazine feature places it on Huggins's property about fifteen years before the article was written

sources.title: Eastover Tower, National Historic Lookout Register

notes_for_editor: Probably the same tower as us-sc-eastover, which records the register's current Huggins/Littlejohn location (33.9497, -80.7017), about 7 km from this record's coordinates (33.953, -80.7811). The coordinates are not checked against any source, so this story does not call them the original site. The register contradicts itself: it says the tower moved to family property in 1995 and also says it had yet to be moved after the 2007 sale. The magazine's nickname for the tower is left out of the story. The P&C article reports the system decommissioned in 1994; the SCFC page says closed 1993, and this story follows SCFC. A footnote was added to the sentence on Huggins's 1995 purchase; the register citation previously covered only the sentence after it.
